title: Chapter 6 – FIDE Rating Regulations: Mock Exam

questions.text: What is the minimum time each player must have for a game to be eligible for FIDE standard rating?
questions.explanation: As per Article B02.1, for a game to be rated by FIDE for standard rating, the rate of play must allow at least 60 minutes for each player to complete all moves.

questions.text: What is the K-factor for a new player in the FIDE rating system?
questions.explanation: As per Article B02.8, the K-factor is 40 for new players, 20 for players below 2400 who are not new, and 10 for established players above 2400. A higher K-factor means ratings change more rapidly.

questions.text: Within how many months of the event must a rating report be submitted to FIDE?
questions.explanation: As per Article B02.4, all rated events must be reported to FIDE within two months of the end of the event. Failure to report within this period may result in the event not being rated.

questions.text: Are rapid and blitz ratings maintained separately from standard ratings?

options.text: No, all ratings are combined into one FIDE rating
Yes, rapid and blitz ratings are each maintained independently
Only blitz is separate; rapid is combined with standard

questions.explanation: As per Article B02-RB, rapid and blitz games are rated separately from standard games. A player's rapid and blitz ratings are maintained independently on separate rating lists.

questions.text: How is a player's expected score (We) used in the FIDE rating calculation?

options.text: We is subtracted from actual score W, then multiplied by K to get the rating change
We is added to actual score W to get the new rating
We is used only for title norm calculations, not rating changes
We determines the K-factor to be applied

questions.explanation: As per Article B02.8, the rating change is K × (W - We), where K is the K-factor, W is the actual score, and We is the expected score based on rating differences between the player and their opponents.

questions.text: What is the minimum number of rated opponents required for a FIDE rated event?
questions.explanation: Per Article B02.2, to be considered for FIDE rating, a player must play against at least 3 rated opponents in the event. Events must also have at least 5 players participating in total.

questions.text: What is the K-factor for a player whose rating has surpassed 2400 for the first time?

options.text: The K-factor remains at 40 for the rest of their career
The K-factor drops to 10 only after completing 30 rated games above 2400
The K-factor changes to 20 once a player reaches 2400, regardless of games played

questions.explanation: Per Article B02.8, once a player's rating reaches 2400, their K-factor drops from 20 to 10 only after they have also completed a minimum of 30 rated games at or above that level. Both conditions must be met.

questions.text: What is the minimum time per player for a game to qualify for FIDE Rapid rating?

options.text: More than 10 minutes but less than 60 minutes

questions.explanation: Per Article B02-RB, Rapid chess is defined as a game where each player has more than 10 minutes but less than 60 minutes for all moves, or a total of more than 10 minutes with an increment. This distinguishes Rapid from both Blitz and Standard.

questions.text: How does the Elo formula calculate the expected score for a player against one opponent?
questions.explanation: Per Article B02.8, the Elo expected score formula is We = 1 / (1 + 10^((Ro - Ra)/400)), where Ra is the player's rating and Ro is the opponent's rating. This gives a probability between 0 and 1 of scoring against that opponent.

questions.text: Which of the following events qualifies a player to earn a FIDE title norm?

options.text: Any club-level event with 10 or more players
Any national championship regardless of player strength
FIDE-approved events with required percentages of titled players
Any blitz tournament with a minimum prize fund

questions.explanation: Per Article B02.5, a title norm can only be achieved in FIDE-approved events that meet specific requirements — including minimum average rating of opponents, required percentages of titled players from different federations, and minimum number of games.
